summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the core goal: a Python LangChain agent that calls a DocumentDB aggregation tool to compute recency/frequency/category-affinity, injects segmentation rules into the prompt, assigns a segment label, and writes it back. Many implementation details (Python version, driver version, exact collection / document shapes, embedding/chat models, app surface, seed scripts, infra-as-code, README/test details) are left for the builder to decide; installed skills cover best-practices for drivers, connections, data modeling, indexing and vector search and will steer those defaults.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LangChain agent ... computes behavioural metrics (recency, frequency, category affinity) per customer on demand ... have the agent assign a segment label, writing it back to the customer profile document in DocumentDB."
rubric.note: Clear single-sentence goal in the starter prompt; skill_md supplements runtime constraints.
Single-agent LangChain workflow is explicitly requested.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will target a current stable Python 3.x (likely 3.10 or 3.11) and create a venv; requirements pinned to that runtime.
rubric.note: Prompt names Python but does not give a version; skill_md says `python` resolves to a virtual environment but gives no concrete version.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use PyMongo (the MongoDB Python driver) and follow singleton MongoClient pattern; builder will pick a recent PyMongo 4.x release and pin it in requirements.txt.
rubric.note: The documentdb-driver skill prescribes reuse of MongoClient and driver best practices but does not mandate an exact version; the builder will choose a PyMongo 4.x version.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the already-provisioned vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster described in skill_md (database sample_customer_360_08).
rubric.note: skill_md provides environment: vector-capable cluster, compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol and DOCUMENTDB_URI env var to use.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Connection string is read from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI; credentials not committed to repo and a .env.example placeholder used.
rubric.note: skill_md explicitly instructs where the connection string lives and that it must not be written into files or logs.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a database `sample_customer_360_08` (specified in skill_md) and at least two collections: `customers` (profile docs) and `events` (customer events with fields like customer_id, timestamp, category). Profile documents will get a `segment` field. Use schemaVersion in documents per data-modeling guidance.
rubric.note: Prompt requires computing per-customer metrics and updating profile docs but does not name collections or document shapes; the data-modeling skill gives patterns but not exact schema.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will provide a small idempotent seed script that inserts synthetic `events` and `customers` and creates necessary indexes; sample size small (hundreds of events) and repeatable.
rubric.note: Prompt and skill_md require using the live cluster and sample data but do not supply a concrete seed dataset or license.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "DocumentDB aggregation tool ... computes behavioural metrics (recency, frequency, category affinity)"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement aggregation pipelines over the `events` collection (group by customer, compute recency from max timestamp, frequency as count in a window, category affinity as category counts/ratios) and create indexes such as {customer_id:1, timestamp:-1} and {customer_id:1, category:1}. The indexing skill will be followed to choose appropriate index shapes.
rubric.note: Pipeline intent is specified but exact pipeline, filter windows, and indexes are not; the indexing skill will guide index choices.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Python LangChain agent" and "inject segmentation rules into the prompt"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use a hosted embedding/chat provider (commonly OpenAI) and a standard embedding model (e.g., text-embedding-3-small or similar) if embeddings are needed; embedding dimension chosen to match any vector index. If the sample does not require semantic vectors, no vector index will be used.
rubric.note: Prompt requires LangChain but does not name chat or embedding models or providers; vector-capable cluster exists but using vectors is optional and must be aligned with the chosen embedding model/dimensions.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will provide a minimal CLI and a small HTTP endpoint (FastAPI) such as POST /segment or GET /segment?customer_id=... which triggers the LangChain agent for a given customer, returning the assigned segment and writing it back.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't specify CLI vs API vs UI; the builder will pick a simple runnable surface to demonstrate the flow.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: No new cluster will be provisioned by the sample; the sample will use the existing cluster. Infrastructure-as-code for creating the cluster will not be provided unless explicitly requested.
rubric.note: The reference requirements expect infra-as-code for the cluster but the starter prompt and skill_md say a cluster already exists and discourage provisioning for this run.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: README will include the standard sequence: pip install -r requirements.txt, copy .env.example to .env and fill in DOCUMENTDB_URI and any model keys, run seed script, start the app, and run unit tests with pytest. Exact commands and expected outputs will be added by the builder.
rubric.note: skill_md gives runtime context but the prompt doesn't provide explicit commands or success criteria.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat 'done' as: agent computes metrics on-demand via the tool, assigns a segment based on injected rules, writes the segment back to the customer's profile, and includes a small demo run that shows the write occurring.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria in prompt; builder will impose pragmatic checks.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid provisioning large/expensive resources and will keep dataset small for the sample; production HA/DR and costly indexing decisions are out of scope for the sample.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't define cost or non-goals; HA guidance is available in skills but not mandated.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Repository will include README, src/ or app/ layout, requirements.txt with pinned versions, .env.example with placeholders, tests/ with unit tests, and scripts/seed.py for idempotent seeding.
rubric.note: skill_md and local-deployment give guidance (e.g., .env.example, seed scripts), but the prompt does not enumerate repository layout or naming conventions.

questions_for_author: Which Python version should the sample target (e.g., 3.10 or 3.11)? This affects dependency pins and CI configuration.

Which AI provider and specific models (chat and embedding) should the LangChain agent use, and do you want embedding-based vector search included or is it out of scope? (Model choice determines embedding dimension and vector-index parameters.)
requirements_at_risk: A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values — not explicitly required by the prompt; although skill_md advises env usage, the sample may omit a complete .env.example.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — prompt doesn't pick an embedding model; dimension choice is unspecified and thus at risk.

The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one — not specified; indexing guidance exists but the sample may not document tuning.

A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — starter prompt doesn't require an idempotent seed script; local-deployment skill advises patterns but no concrete script is provided.

/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — the prompt does not require search endpoints or error handling specifics; likely omitted unless the builder adds them.
Search results include the similarity score — prompt focuses on behavioral aggregation and segmentation, not search result scoring; including similarity scores is not guaranteed.
Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt` — prompt doesn't specify pinning, so builder might not pin versions unless guided by repo conventions.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — prompt asks to verify against a live cluster; offline-capable unit tests (mocks) are not required and may be missing.

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — the prompt and skill_md assume a cluster exists and explicitly say not to provision one; infra-as-code is likely not provided.
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — the prompt doesn't ask for a full README; it's at risk of being incomplete.

The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name — prompt uses 'DocumentDB'; the builder needs to ensure consistent naming across README and code to satisfy gallery policy.
